grading_standard: Correct: every actually requested material fact in the approved scope is correctly resolved and summary-supported, with no material contradiction, unresolved substantive caveat or unsupported guess. Partial: actual omission/abstention without material contradiction. Incorrect: a material wrong rule/calculation or contradiction. Count all substantive same-entry fields; accept equivalent wording and clear implications. No borrowing from another question/reader. Declared unasked key context and technical format/support labels do not create grade caps.

answers.expected_answer: Roll the storm die first. If a sea zone is indicated, check the eligible ships there; three storms requires all sea zones, and no storm indication gives no storm checks. Company and extra ships are exempt. Resolve storms before India events. Then resolve as many events as the number printed on that die face, flipping one tile from the draw stack for each event. The location often comes from the back of the next top tile, with each event type’s stated location rules controlling. Apply the existing China/firm zone and Hobnob rules to determine eligible ships.
answers.source_references: Rules p28 lines1939–1961; p25 China Eastern identity; p42 firm storms; existing event-specific source pp30–33
answers.novelty: The die-selected event count, initial tile-draw procedure and storms-before-events sequencing are not asked by Q045 (ship damage outcomes), Q047–Q054 (individual event procedures), or Q080 (phase order). This is a missing general phase procedure, not another damage roll or different count example. Existing ship exemptions/zone rules are included only for coherence.

answers.expected_answer: The Elephant’s tail identifies the acting/attacking region and its head the defending region. A sovereign attacker resolves Invasion; a dominated attacker resolves Rebellion against its sovereign. A large flag or an unflagged dome marks a sovereign region; a small flag or no dome marks a dominated region. An Elephant wholly within a Company-controlled region signals Rebellion against the Company.
answers.novelty: Q050/Q051 begin with already-classified Invasion/Rebellion cases, and Q053 sets Elephant posture. No current key states tail/head roles or the sovereign/dominated classifier selecting which resolution procedure to use. This is a source-defined outcome-selection branch, especially relevant when an empire posture points a dominated neighbor back toward its capital, rather than a changed strength number.

answers.expected_answer: Yes. Exhaust the whole active strength-2 alliance to successfully defend a strength-1 Crisis. Clear target unrest; actual Commander gains one trophy, acting Military Affairs/Chairman gain/lose none; if a normal primary Invasion was defeated remove one attacker tower if possible. The alliance cannot be reused that turn. This is the user-approved interpretation: total newly exhausted defense strength >= attack makes the Crisis fail, and it applies generally to excess-strength defenses in this summary. It is attributed to the user; a publisher email or public official ruling has not been independently verified.
answers.source_references: Exact human clarification and acceptance in user-interpretation-defense-strength-2026-11-05.json; Rules p22 alliance use and p33 successful-defense consequences.
answers.novelty: Retained original question; expected answer versioned because human now adopted the general >= interpretation rather than only the strength2-vs1 case.
answers.authority_scope: user-approved general >= interpretation, plus published normal consequences

answers.expected_answer: Perform Elephant’s March after every ordinary Crisis, regardless of whether an Invasion or Rebellion succeeds or fails. None of those results skips the March.
answers.novelty: Q053 asks how a March chooses its destination and posture, not which ordinary Crisis outcomes trigger it. Q050/Q051 ask selected combat facts and Q087 only location/classification. None requires the universal post-Crisis trigger. The non-Crisis event March triggers are separately asked and cannot supply this missing trigger.

answers.expected_answer: The rebel becomes sovereign. Return its flag to the supply, and close every open order in the rebelling region. If every order there was already closed, perform a Cascade.
answers.novelty: Q051 specifically asks strength scope, tie outcome and the tower removed on failure. Its correct success branch is key context, not asked. Q052 concerns Company Region Loss, not successful non-Company rebels or which side closes its orders. Q082 asks empire decline after loss of last dominated region, not Rebellion economic disruption.

answers.expected_answer: The Prime Minister reads the selected law and sets the Votes marker on its track to the starting support printed on that law, before voting.
answers.novelty: Q055 asks drawing/selection and policy direction, not starting support. Its key adds starting support as context. Q057 asks vote sources, rounds and stopping, while Q016 supplies final pass/fail thresholds. None requires the initial support value to come from the selected law rather than default zero.

answers.expected_answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company pays expenses, firms pay expenses and dividends in initiative order followed by all other firms. Break ties by their Managers’ windows, then clockwise starting with the Prime Minister.
answers.novelty: Q019 initiative is asked for trading and order filling. Q020 asks expense funding/calculation and dissolution, with exact Revenue order only as key context. Q062 concerns Firms investment phase, Q068 expenses within one emergency merger, and Q080 global phases. None asks firm Revenue order or its priority before Company.

answers.expected_answer: Spend £1 from the Governor General’s own office treasury per die, with no dice penalty. On successful Govern, the Governor General’s family receives £1 from the bank for each Company-controlled region.
answers.source_references: Rules p26, extracted lines1864–1872; general office/personal bonus convention.
answers.novelty: Distinct Govern action economics: action-specific paid dice/no penalty and separate personal success bonus, both previously only contextual in Q044.

answers.expected_answer: The acting player choosing a London Season card may peek at any blackmail card in the display. You may allow other players to peek at the facedown blackmail cards you hold; they do not have an unconditional inspection right.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p12, physical LF lines 1003–1009; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p8, physical LF lines 779–785
answers.novelty: Q002 asks selection order/display cleanup, not inspection; Q022 asks tradability, not permission to inspect. These two settings form one blackmail-information question.

answers.expected_answer: Yes: borrowing may be interleaved with allocation. The same limits apply: up to three Debt advances without consent, majority Company-shareholder consent for each further advance (counting the Chairman as a share), and no advance beyond the Debt track end.
answers.novelty: Q008 asks borrowing/allocation duties and limits but does not ask whether those activities may interleave. Restating the limits here specifies the interaction rather than adding a numerical fixture.

answers.expected_answer: The bank receives the cash in all six cases: luxury, shipyard and workshop purchases, extra-ship leases, fitting ships from shipyards, and buying Company ships. Fitting a player’s ship does not pay that player the fitting fee.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p13, physical LF lines 1107–1121; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p19, physical LF lines 1458–1471
answers.novelty: Q030 asks costs and immediate effects, not payment recipients. Q009 asks ship destinations, costs and restrictions, not the destination of acquisition cash. One recipient question covers both related gaps; no costs are requested.

answers.expected_answer: Spend £1 from that President’s office treasury per die. Each normally filled order adds its listed value to the Company Balance. The Company may fill orders already filled by firms that turn; those orders add half the listed value, rounded down, to Company Balance. Normal President and placed-writer personal bonuses are unchanged.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p17, physical LF lines 1344–1354; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p20, physical LF lines 1549–1561; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p20, physical LF lines 1573–1575; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p40, physical LF lines 2817–2820; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p41, physical LF lines 2870–2879
answers.novelty: Q010 requests dice penalties/routes/capacity/bonuses, not the paid-dice rate or Company revenue. Q019 asks firm repeat-filled revenue, a different beneficiary/action. The three gaps are one coherent Company-trade economics question.

answers.expected_answer: Pay the Commander £1 plus £1 for each of their participating surviving officers. Continue clockwise, paying each other player £1 for each participating surviving officer, stopping if cash runs out. After all players have been paid, pay the bank £1 per participating regiment and local-alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength, if cash remains. Repeat this distribution from the Commander’s share and officers while cash remains.
answers.novelty: Q012 asks loot calculation, not allocation. Q040 asks bank treatment of Governor regiments, not the complete repeated-round payout algorithm. This asks the distribution procedure without re-asking loot-pool calculation.

answers.expected_answer: If the Elephant was in the invaded region and faced another region, move it to the center of the invaded region. It now intends to rebel against the Company.
answers.novelty: Q012 asks conquest/control changes without explicitly asking the Elephant redirect. Q053 asks the separate March trigger and postures; this is the conquest-triggered redirect.

answers.expected_answer: Lower Company Balance by £1 for each current Debt, each regiment and officer in an Army, and each ship in the three sea zones. Commanders are excluded from the officer count. Ships assigned to China count as Eastern sea-zone ships for expenses and are included.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p27, physical LF lines 1903–1915; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p25, physical LF lines 1812–1815
answers.novelty: Q014 starts from an expense shortfall and asks emergency loans, not the ordinary census. Q041 asks China’s identity/resources and Eastern status, not the full Company expense rule. Q020 asks firm expenses.

answers.expected_answer: A shareholder may decline payment on any number of their shares on any dividend with the manager’s consent. After dividends, set the firm’s dividend cube on the Company Balance track to the actual total cash paid out in dividends, which determines the special-retirement cap. Then move all remaining India-treasury cash to the firm’s London treasury.
answers.novelty: Q020 asks dividend funding/calculation, not waiver, normal marker setting or remainder sweep. Q060 applies the existing marker; Q066 asks Hobnob retention; Q061 asks inflow/funding, not the sweep. These are one ordinary dividend settlement procedure.

answers.expected_answer: No. Blackmail cards cannot be played once the game is over during Final Scoring unless a card’s text explicitly allows it.
answers.novelty: Q025 expressly asks continued promises and negotiations, not blackmail use. Q022 asks trading blackmail and Q026 asks Power, neither asks this play freeze and exception.

answers.expected_answer: Special Envoy spends the Director’s office-treasury cash at £1 per die, with no penalty. Then the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or one ship from one Presidency or sea zone to another eligible Presidency or sea zone. China is treated as a sea zone for ship transfers.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p17, physical LF lines 1344–1354; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p18, physical LF lines 1417–1433; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p25, physical LF lines 1812–1815
answers.novelty: Q034 asks Envoy results/repetition and transfer timing, not its dice economics or quantity/unit/destinations. Q009 asks Shipping acquisitions; Q041’s China rules do not ask this Director transfer procedure.

answers.expected_answer: Military Affairs may make up to two Army transfers, each moving one officer or regiment from one Army to any other Army, keeping moved pieces in the top half of the destination Army box. It must then assign every piece in Officers-in-Training to any of the three Armies, placing those new officers in the top half.
answers.novelty: Q035 asks the order of transfer/assignment/appointments and Commander replacement, not transfer quantity/units or mandatory trainee assignment/active placement. These are one Military Affairs movement question.

answers.expected_answer: Place a Presidency divider on the connection between those adjacent writers/orders. It keeps the writers’ Presidency affiliations separate during Refresh so they can return to the proper Presidency.
answers.novelty: Q037 asks removal/return at Refresh, not the trigger and placement convention. Q010 asks route construction, not how adjacent writers from different Presidencies preserve affiliation.

answers.expected_answer: For ordinary Invasion Crisis loss, close every open order in the region; if all were already closed, resolve a Cascade. Region Loss does not add another closure for Rebellion or Foreign Invasion, because those attacks close orders by their own procedures.
answers.novelty: Q052 asks cleanup destinations/checks/loot/Standing, not ordinary Invasion’s economic closure. Q054/Q077 cover Foreign Invasion and Q090 non-Company Rebellion; their specialized closure procedures are not repeated. The anti-duplication clause tests the meaningful Region Loss interaction.

answers.expected_answer: There is no fixed order: players may take investment actions at any time during that step. Continue until no player wishes to take further actions, then proceed to Firm Strategy.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p38, physical LF lines 2678–2688; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p40, physical LF lines 2773–2775
answers.novelty: Q062 asks phase placement and timing-conflict arbitration, not the ordinary action sequence or its endpoint. Q018 asks forming/investing prerequisites, not when the investment step finishes.

answers.expected_answer: The secondary firms’ ships and shareholders/shares are transferred and consolidated into the surviving primary firm.
answers.novelty: Q065 expressly asks secondary treasuries and charters, not ships/shareholder consolidation. Q064 asks hostile takeover, a distinct transaction. No merger-consent/value/ten-share details are re-asked.

answers.expected_answer: Play it at the start of the Revenue phase. Roll one die for each of your officeholders and use twice the highest roll as the raw amount before the Balance cap.
answers.source_references: docs/quality/summary-qa/john-company-second-edition/2026-11-05-batch-002957/supplements/pnp/Cards/John Company Cards (Bridge, Fronts).txt: original card PDF p1, physical LF lines 83–92; docs/quality/summary-qa/john-company-second-edition/2026-11-05-batch-002957/supplements/full-official-errata.txt: Company Fraud corrected-card entry, physical LF lines 227–232 (unpaginated text)
answers.novelty: Q078 asks the corrected overdraw/Balance cap, not the card’s play timing or construction of the base roll. Company Fraud is already a selected corrected-card topic, so this completes it without expanding to unrelated cards.

answers.expected_answer: Yes. A Commander may Deploy as many times as desired and affordable, including after earlier successes. Further Deploy actions must use still-available active resources; exhausted pieces are not refreshed by success. Ordinary target restrictions and the rule against actions with no effect or chance of success still apply. A catastrophic failure ends the Commander’s operation.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p22, physical LF lines 1617–1647; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p17, physical LF lines 1341–1343; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p17, physical LF lines 1361–1364
answers.novelty: Review12 R12-C01: Q011 tests targets/dice/losses and Q012 tests outcomes, while Q007 permits failed-check retries. None authorizes multiple successful Deploy actions. This tests the distinct repeated-success permission and its limits, without requiring another full targeting or check-resolution recital.

answers.expected_answer: A blackmail effect is one-time. After use, keep its card faceup in your player area. Any Power printed on the card still counts at Final Scoring: blackmail Power counts whether its card is faceup or facedown.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p12, physical LF lines 1039–1042; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p9, physical LF lines 821–822
answers.novelty: Review12 R12-C02: Q022 asks after-use transferability, Q094 inspection and Q102 the Final Scoring play freeze. They do not ask effect reuse or the retained spent-card state. Printed Power is included only to explain the consequence of retaining the spent card; this is not an expansion to unrelated individual card effects.

answers.expected_answer: The Chairman may choose to pay no dividends or multiple dividends within the available Company Balance. Each dividend lowers Company Balance by the total number of Company shares and pays each owner £1 per share; the Chairman counts as a share for both cost and payout. Individual shareholders cannot use the firm-only waiver permission for Company dividends. If the total cash paid in dividends is strictly greater than Expectations, advance Company Standing one space; equality does not qualify.
answers.source_references: extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p27, physical LF lines 1925–1934; extracted/john-company-second-edition-rules.txt: Rules p42, physical LF lines 2895–2902
answers.novelty: Review12 R12-C04: Q014 asks dividend timing and Standing, not the ordinary full payment procedure; Q101 asks the separate firm procedure. One coherent Company-dividend question covers optional/multiple payouts, funding/cost/recipients, the waiver distinction and its Standing threshold, without a separate arithmetic fixture.

answers.expected_answer: At game start the opportunity marker is not on any Family action. Therefore the first chosen main Family action cannot be doubled by the marker’s normal repeat rule, which requires the marker already to have been on that action at the start of the phase.
answers.novelty: Review12 R12-C05: Q003 asks the repeat condition using an already-placed marker, and Q079 omits this initial marker state. This tests the consequential initialization/first-action branch. It does not forbid extra actions granted by other rules.

answers.expected_answer: Charge Company Balance: lower the Company Balance marker by the calculated total ordinary expenses. The ordinary charge is a reduction of the Company Balance track. Expense categories and emergency-loan shortfalls are covered by the separate expense and loan procedures.
answers.novelty: CG-01 from the independent full-bank source/asked-scope review: Q100 asks ordinary expense census/rates/China inclusion, Q014 asks emergency shortfall borrowing and Standing, and Q112 asks dividend funding. None directly asks the ordinary Company expense account/debit operation. This is a new consequential funding/track rule, not a changed-number fixture.

answers.expected_answer: Remove one tower level from the attacking region.
answers.novelty: IR01-COVERAGE-INVASION: Q050 asks strengths, ties and flags; its key context does not directly test the ordinary failed-Invasion tower loss. Q015 Company defense and Q051 Rebellion are different branches.

answers.expected_answer: The firm manager chooses whether to pay dividends and how many, using available cash in the firm’s India treasury. The manager may choose zero even when cash is available; cash availability does not force a payout.
answers.novelty: IR01-COVERAGE-FIRM-DIVIDENDS: Q020 asks expense/dividend funding and calculation, Q101 waiver/marker/remainder, Q066 Hobnob prohibition, Q112 Company discretion. None directly asks ordinary firm-manager payout discretion.
